messages:
Ravi: Throwing an idea into the ring: define an "attestable parcel format" (APF) tailored for air-gapped/on‑prem upgrades. Goals: inspectable on removable media, partial apply for constrained nodes, and provable possession for staged rollouts.
Sasha: Nice. How does APF differ from previous "bundle" concepts?
Ravi: Emphasis on operator ergonomics: (1) micro-manifest that can be read without specialized tooling, (2) chunk-level possession proofs so a relay can attest which shards a node already has, (3) explicit activation semantics to allow zero-downtime rollback.
Lina: signer lifecycle question: if parcels are signed, how do we safely rotate keys for already distributed parcels?
Tom: For air-gapped sites we can't rely on live CRLs. Proposal: parcel header carries signer metadata + a compact signed rotation-history appendix. Operators get a signed rotation snapshot periodically via secure channels, or they can maintain a local trust file.
Sasha: UX: operator should be able to plug a USB and run `rbox parcel inspect-lite /mnt/usb/update.apf` and immediately see version, criticality, chunk-summary, and required disk. No need to extract.
Ravi: Exactly; 'inspect-lite' prints a tiny JSON-like table: header, list of top-level components (core weights, tokenizer, optional plugins), and a small digest of proofs.
Lina: proofs worry me for giant models naive Merkle proofs could be huge. We should design proofs proportional to changed-chunk-count. Use a chunk-level Merkle, then encode only paths for changed leaves.
Tom: For fast checks we could support 'sampled proofs' (e.g., verify 1% of changed leaves) for quick integrity gating, but require full proofs before activation. Sampling helps when operator wants to triage USBs quickly.
Sasha: Edge case: some customers want to apply partial model updates (e.g., core quantized weights first, then expansion layers). APF should declare 'apply phases' with dependency graph so nodes can stage minimal critical pieces first.
Ravi: Implementation plan: two activation slots (A/B). APF apply streams changed chunks into the B slot; once verification & sanity checks pass, atomic pointer flip. Rollback = flip pointer back. This avoids re-pull for rollback but requires retention of previous chunks until GC.
Lina: GC policy needs definition: keep N historical versions or time-based retention. Also need per-tenant quotas to avoid disk exhaustion attacks.
Tom: Speaking of attacks: adversary could craft APF with millions of tiny chunks to exhaust verifier CPU/memory. Mitigations: enforce max-chunk-count, min-chunk-size, and a worst-case cost estimator evaluated during inspect. Reject parcels exceeding policy.
Sasha: We also need telemetry hooks: when a site rejects a parcel due to policy, Console should surface why (too many chunks, signature mismatch, stale signer).
Ravi: On Dedicated deployments we can host a 'verifier service' that pre-validates parcels and provides a compact attestation token the on-prem node trusts. Private/offline customers without that can use the local sidecar verifier.
Lina: Testing: add lab tests that simulate USB delivery, sampled proof checks, rotation snapshots, and a throughput test for verifier to set perf budgets.
Tom: CLI samples:
```
# pack a parcel (signed)
rbox parcel pack --components model:v3,tokenizer:1.2 --signer=corp-kms --out=update.apf
# lightweight inspect on USB
rbox parcel inspect-lite /media/usb/update.apf
# full verify and dry-run apply
rbox parcel verify --trusted-keys=/etc/rbox/trust.json /media/usb/update.apf
rbox parcel apply --slot=b --dry-run /media/usb/update.apf
# activate after checks
rbox parcel activate --slot=b
```
Sasha: Operator playbook reqs: preflight checklist, max-chunk thresholds, safe-rollback steps, how to rotate trust bundle offline. Lina + Ravi want to own docs?
Lina: I can draft the playbook sections for rotation + offline trust bundle. Ravi takes parcel format appendix and inspect examples.
ops-bot: Note: Architecture sync scheduled 2024-11-09 09:30 (link).
Tom: Action items: (1) RFC appendix with format spec + examples, (2) QA harness for USB/offline rotation, (3) Console telemetry design for parcel rejections. I'll open tickets and link owners. :thumbsup:
